title: Ekta Kapoor Wants Her Stars in Jail. Farah Khan and Riteish Deshmukh Hold the Keys When 'Lock Upp 2' Lands on Netflix.
excerpt: Fourteen inmates, six weeks, and a confessional that has already produced the year's most unhinged press launch. Sach Ya Sazaa storms Netflix on June 27.
body:
There is a particular kind of chaos that only **Ekta Kapoor** can manufacture, and on a Mumbai stage this week it arrived fully formed: a producer announcing, with a straight face, that she has spent fifteen years collecting people she would like to throw behind bars. "There comes a point when a producer thinks, *inko toh jail mein daalna hi hoga*," she said, and the room roared, because everyone knew she half meant it.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=F4yMI_Qh6ug</youtube>

That is the premise of **Lock Upp 2: Sach Ya Sazaa**, the prison-themed reality juggernaut that storms **Netflix on June 27**. Four years after Kangana Ranaut presided over the original on MX Player and ALTBalaji, the format has been scrubbed up, scaled up, and handed to two new jailers who could not be more perfectly cast: **Farah Khan** and **Riteish Deshmukh**. Fourteen celebrity inmates. Six weeks of confinement. Basic necessities to be earned, secrets to be confessed, and a viewing audience invited to play judge, jury, and warden.

If the launch event is any indication, the producers have already won. Farah Khan, asked why her husband Shirish Kunder would not be an inmate, deadpanned that she handles his sentencing privately: "*Uski saza main usko ghar pe deti hoon!*" Then she turned philosophical about her own qualifications for the jailer's chair, and it was, frankly, the truest thing anyone said all evening.

> "All directors have a jailer in them. When you're on set, you're literally a jailer because you're controlling everything there — you're putting people in their places, whether they are stars or technicians." — Farah Khan

She's not wrong. The woman has marshalled hundred-dancer item numbers and Shah Rukh Khan's shirtless abs into submission; a few misbehaving reality contestants are a Tuesday. Riteish Deshmukh, meanwhile, leaned into the host's diplomatic crouch. Asked whether he'd love to lock up Salman Khan or Sanjay Dutt, he demurred with a grin — "My duty is to host" — which is exactly what someone says when they would, in fact, very much enjoy locking up Salman Khan.

And then there was **Ram Kapoor**, who detonated the evening's most quotable grenade. Reflecting on the on-again-off-again chemistry of his fifteen-year working relationship with Ekta Kapoor, he announced that the universe kept sending him signs to join the show — before veering, with magnificent disregard for the room, into: "*Ekta jaanti hai ki Ram ko maine bina chaddi ke dekha hai!*" Farah, ever the floor manager, shot back: "I hope you'll wear a *chaddi* inside the show." This is the energy. This is the entire pitch.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZbxWWVBIe-/


The inmate roster is being released in teasing drips, and it's a canny mix of soap royalty and tabloid catnip. The first three confirmed names — model and *Desi Bling* personality **Pamela Serena**, television titan **Ram Kapoor**, and *Yeh Rishta Kya Kehlata Hai* favourite **Shivangi Joshi** — landed on June 22. Industry chatter adds **Harshad Chopda**, **Sunita Ahuja** (who never met a microphone she didn't want to detonate), *Sasural Simar Ka*'s **Dheeraj Dhoopar**, the *Splitsvilla* alumnae, and — the casting masterstroke — **Madhuri Grover**, wife of Shark Tank India's most meme-able mentor Ashneer Grover. If you wanted a season engineered to trend every single morning, this is the lineup you'd build.

What makes Lock Upp work, and what made the first season a genuine breakout, is its refusal to be polite. The format strips away the gloss of a Bigg Boss living room and replaces it with scarcity, surveillance, and forced confession. Inmates barter for food and sleep; they're hauled into a confession box and asked to trade their dirtiest secrets for survival. It is, by design, undignified — and that's the point. With Netflix's Tudum machinery now behind it, the reach goes global, which means the diaspora gets a front-row seat to the year's messiest Hindi watercooler show without a single VPN workaround.

For NRI viewers across the **US, UK, Canada, and Australia, Lock Upp 2: Sach Ya Sazaa streams on Netflix from June 27**, in Hindi with subtitles, dropping new episodes in the platform's signature binge-friendly cadence. Bigg Boss 20 looms later this year, and Karan Johar's *Traitors* Season 2 is circling Prime Video, but for now the reality crown is Ekta's to lose.

Six weeks. Fourteen egos. One Farah Khan with a clipboard and zero patience. Lock the door.
